page: Microsoft Azure D2pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture. Powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz, the instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with a single thread per core. The memory subsystem consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core, backed by 128 MB of shared L3 cache. Hyper-V serves as the underlying hypervisor. Storage capabilities include a bundled 118 GB local NVMe solid-state drive alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is present via dedicated AES support.

Benchmark results highlight clear performance characteristics divided between single-thread efficiency and constrained multi-core throughput. Single-threaded data compression represents a distinct strength, with gzip compression reaching 33.01 GB/sec. The instance also delivers midrange single-core results, scoring 1673.0 in Geekbench and 2072.67 in stress-ng. However, the 2-core hardware scale inherently limits multi-core capacity, resulting in lower comparative scores across multi-threaded stress-ng (4121.76) and multi-core Geekbench (3059.0). Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 45.96 GB/sec, while write operations reach 21.07 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput measures 4.18 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput peaks at 4.0 GB/sec.

The qualitative efficiency of the D2pds_v6 profile stems from dedicated ARM core allocation paired with fast onboard NVMe scratch space. The absence of SMT eliminates thread contention on the physical cores. While large data processing and heavy multi-threaded compilations exceed its compute ceiling, the instance is well matched for lightweight microservices, small web servers, background task processors, continuous integration runners, and edge caching layers requiring fast temporary local disk access.
description: Microsoft Azure D2pds_v6 is an ARM-based general-purpose instance powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per physical core, 8.0 GB of system memory, 128 MB of L3 cache, and a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system supports AES hardware encryption. Synthetic benchmarks reveal capable single-thread performance, highlighted by strong gzip compression at 33.01 GB/sec and average single-core scores in Geekbench and stress-ng. Because the core count is limited to two physical cores, multi-threaded throughput and memory write bandwidth occupy lower performance percentiles, with Redis SET operations achieving 4.18 million operations per second. The balanced 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio combined with high-speed local NVMe storage makes this configuration appropriate for lightweight microservices, entry-level web serving, basic CI/CD jobs, and small caching workloads.
